definition: Automated negotiation is a form of interaction in systems that are composed of multiple autonomous agents, in which the aim is to reach agreements through an iterative process of making offers.
details: Automated negotiation can be employed for many tasks human negotiators regularly engage in, such as bargaining and joint decision making. The main topics in automated negotiation revolve around the design of protocols and negotiating strategies.

explainer.lead: Automated negotiation lets autonomous software agents work toward an agreement by exchanging offers. It matters because tasks such as bargaining and joint decision making can be handled through structured interaction rather than a single agent deciding alone.

tiers.eli5: Imagine two friends trading snacks: one makes an offer, the other answers, and they keep going until both like the deal. Automated negotiation gives computer agents a similar way to exchange offers and follow shared rules while trying to agree.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer applies it in a multi-agent system by defining a negotiation protocol and giving each autonomous agent a strategy for making and responding to offers. The main design challenges are the interaction rules and the agents' negotiating strategies.
tiers.paperLevel: Automated negotiation is iterative offer-based interaction among multiple autonomous agents whose aim is agreement. Its central research topics are protocol design and negotiating strategies for tasks including bargaining and joint decision making.

explainer.example: Two autonomous agents bargain over a price. The seller offers 100, the buyer offers 80, and successive offers bring them to 90, where both accept the agreement.

usedIn.name: Bargaining
usedIn.detail: Agents exchange offers in an effort to reach a mutually acceptable deal.

usedIn.name: Joint decision making
usedIn.detail: Autonomous participants negotiate instead of relying on one participant to make the decision.

usedIn.name: Multi-agent systems
usedIn.detail: Negotiation provides a form of interaction between the system's autonomous agents.

explainer.intuition: Several independent agents may need one agreement without any single agent simply choosing for everyone. Negotiation gives them rules for exchanging offers and strategies for moving toward that agreement.
howItWorks: Multiple autonomous agents take part under a shared protocol.
An agent makes an offer according to its negotiating strategy.
Other agents respond with further offers through the iterative process.
The interaction aims to end with an agreement.
explainer.whyItMatters: It gives autonomous agents a structured way to bargain and make joint decisions. Protocols and strategies are therefore central to making the interaction work.
misconceptions: It is not a single decision made by one agent; it involves multiple autonomous agents.
It is not just one offer; negotiation is an iterative process of making offers.
The negotiating strategies and interaction protocols are distinct design topics.
